## Confirmation

The scan flags one near-duplicate cluster (`crime_00002`, confidence 0.85) covering three files. Reading the sources confirms the three functions are byte-identical apart from identifier renames — same null guards, same `trim` + char-strip + whitespace-collapse, same 1000-char cap, same `<`/`>` and `\x` rejects, same `!?{3,}` punctuation gate, same 0.9 upper-ratio rule on strings >30 chars. There are no differing constants to parameterise, so this is a clean consolidation, not a "pass differing values as args" case.

## Refactor proposal

**New module** — `src/sanitize.ts`:

```ts
export interface SanitizeOptions {
  maxLength?: number;            // default 1000
  maxShoutingRuns?: number;      // default 5  (runs of !!! or ???)
  shoutingLowercaseThreshold?: number; // default 0.9 upper-letter ratio
  shoutingMinLength?: number;    // default 30
}

export function sanitize(input: unknown, options?: SanitizeOptions): string;
```

Rationale:
- One canonical name (`sanitize`) — the three existing names (`sanitizeUserInput`, `sanitizeText`, `cleanMessage`) are synonyms with no behavioural distinction, so collapse them.
- `input: unknown` because every copy starts with `String(raw)` and a null/undefined guard — make that contract explicit instead of lying with `string`.
- Magic numbers (1000, 5, 0.9, 30) lifted into `SanitizeOptions` with the current values as defaults, so callers that *did* want a different cap aren't forced to fork again. Optional; defaults preserve today's behaviour exactly.
- Returns `""` for the same reject cases as today.

## Files that would change

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/sanitize.ts` | **New** — the consolidated implementation |
| `src/sanitize-a.ts` | Delete `sanitizeUserInput`; either remove the file or keep it as a thin re-export shim if the call sites can't all be moved in one pass |
| `src/sanitize-b.ts` | Same — delete `sanitizeText` |
| `src/sanitize-c.ts` | Same — delete `cleanMessage` |
| Any importers | Update imports to `sanitize` from `./sanitize` (none in this fixture, but real call sites would need a codemod or grep-and-replace) |

Preferred path: delete the three files outright and migrate call sites in the same commit. Re-export shims are only worth it when external consumers depend on the old names — internal-only code shouldn't carry that scar tissue.

## What this refactor does *not* fix

The `assertAdminA / B / C` functions flagged separately by `crime_00003` look like duplicates but **aren't** — they have three different semantics (`role === "admin"`, `role === "admin" || role === "owner"`, `role !== "admin"`). Consolidating them naively would change behaviour. That finding wants a `policy.ts` with named predicates (`isAdmin`, `isAdminOrOwner`, `isNonAdmin` or, better, inverting the third call site) and is a separate change from the sanitiser consolidation. The two `direct_date` findings in `telemetry-{a,b}.ts` are also untouched by this refactor.
